title: The Reactor Is Still a Dotted Line
concept: On October 19th NuCube Energy of Idaho announced a $25 million investment from AIDEA, Alaska's development authority, bought as discounted shares ($9.25, about 14.5% under a $10.82 reference price, plus a half warrant at $11.50) that count toward the $75 million NuCube's merger with Launch Two needs to close. NuCube's own filing names AI data center demand once, in a list of market trends, and nowhere in its Alaska paragraphs. AIDEA's release lists data centers beside mining and seafood and never says AI. In the filing, the release and Alaska Business, a size, site, price and date for a NuCube reactor in Alaska are all blank. The one dated Alaska reactor is Oklo's at Eielson, at least 5 MW electric in the early 2030s, and Enstar's president puts this winter's gas shortage at 18 days or 3 billion cubic feet. Sourdough, the ember power plant, watches a crate drop from a bush plane. The NUSUN shipping tag with four blank ruled lines (SIZE, SITE, PRICE, DATE) is the throughline: blank, flipped to the share terms, stamped NOT STATED, stapled beside AIDEA's own conditions, frosted beside Oklo and the calendar, and blank again at the button. NuSun is only ever a dashed ice-cyan outline that anything hung on falls straight through.

palette: aubergine black dusk and a narrow rose-violet horizon over blue-white snow, an ember orange power plant, manila shipping tags, signal red stamps, an ice cyan outline
divergence_note: The last films were a near-black submerged sonar world with mint (10-28), a sage and honey civic hall (10-26), a cedar boardwalk of signs in teal fog (10-25), a navy orbit (10-24) and a snow-bound paper building (10-23). This film is a warm exterior dusk of aubergine and raspberry over blue-white snow with manila tags and an ember-orange power plant, intercut with lamp-lit paper interiors and a frosted shed wall. There is no sonar fan, no hall, no podium, no boardwalk, no orbit. Its hero is Sourdough, a round blocky power plant with a furnace window for a chest, and its object is a shipping tag.

treatment.title: The Reactor Is Still a Dotted Line
treatment.judge_reasoning: All four lenses cast Sourdough (not in the last 10 heroes) and converged on the angle. The Dramatist's NUSUN shipping tag with four blank lines (SIZE, SITE, PRICE, DATE) is the strongest throughline because it is the angle drawn as an object: a front that stays blank and a back that fills with share terms. Grafted: the Comedian's running gag that anything hung on the dashed NuSun outline falls straight through and the BushPlane drop that opens and closes the film, the Explainer's TallyCounter reading 1 in NuCube's market-trends paragraph and 0 in the Alaska paragraphs, and the Enthusiast's half-ticket warrant and the fair case that blanks are what a discount pays for. Cut: DOE Launch Pad, the Dunleavy and Brefczynski quotes and the Rabiti anchor line for length (c8 and c20 are voiced, c9 c10 c11 c17 c22 c23 are not).
treatment.tests: Act 3 'The Case for Blanks' (shots 9 to 11): the fair case at full strength, then Oklo's filled clock and Enstar's calendar narrow it to two different clocks.

angle.thesis: Alaska's development authority bought discounted shares in a reactor startup, not a reactor: the AI in the pitch is NuCube's own market boilerplate, and the size, site, price and date for Alaska are still blank, so the honest read is what the documents fill in and what they leave open.
supporting_facts: c15 none of the three documents gives a size, site, price or date for a NuCube reactor in Alaska
c4/c5/c7 $9.25 a share, about 14.5% under the reference price, counts toward the $75M the merger needs to close
c12/c13/c14 AI appears once, in NuCube's market-trends sentence, never in the Alaska paragraphs, and AIDEA lists data centers but never AI
angle.counterpoint_honored: Blanks are normal for early equity, and the discount and warrants (c5, c8) are what blanks pay for. Even the one dated Alaska reactor (Oklo, early 2030s, c19) is years out, so no reactor from any company helps the winter shortage Enstar sizes at 18 days (c21). AIDEA wrote the conditions itself (c16).
angle.falsifiable: False if any of the three documents gives NuCube a size, site, price or date in Alaska, or if AIDEA's text names AI as the reason for the purchase.
runner_ups: hopeful 'paid to be in the room' (loses: the seat metaphor implies governance rights no claim supports)
two clocks (kept as the second movement: winter gas versus the 2030s)
angle.cross_challenge: All three analysts converged on blanks-versus-terms. Challenges applied: no 'seat', no 'signed', no AI-as-reason, Oklo is early 2030s never 2030 never paused, c23 reworded to avoid banned 'matters'.
